Definition: from the base of G3466; to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach:--instruct.
BiblicalUsage: Myeo means to be initiated, to be taught by experience — Paul says, I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. In the Greek text the form stands under the lemma μυέομαι, spelled differently from this study's headword.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's instruction is the whole Christian life in one verse: taught by plenty and by want, and content in both.
